Subject: Hosted API pricing — commit tiers + burst behavior

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A few follow-ups from procurement and finance: they want clarity on how Redwood handles (a) minimum monthly commit across tiers, (b) surges/bursts above commit (we expect seasonal spikes), and (c) a grace/true-up mechanism if usage overshoots for a single month.

Specifically: can we get: 1) a worked example showing cost with a 500k token/month commit and a 3x burst in month 6, 2) the overage rate applied to bursts (is it the on-demand per-token price or a negotiated overage), and 3) whether you offer a short grace window (e.g., 30 days) before we get invoiced for true-ups?

We want to keep the model simple for internal forecasting but need some protections to avoid large unexpected bills.

Simon

BrightCart

Hi Simon — thanks for laying out the asks, and great meeting yesterday. I pulled together a short worked example and our recommended commit structure. See summary below and attached worksheet.

Quick summary (assumptions):
- Commit: 500k input+output tokens / month at Tier A effective rate $0.0008 per token.
- On-demand rate (no commit): $0.0020 per token.
- Negotiated overage (on top of commit): 1.5x the committed rate for burst capacity = $0.0012/token.
- Burst protection: monthly burst allowance equal to 2x commit (so for 500k commit, first 500k covered by commit, next 500k within burst allowance billed at negotiated overage; anything beyond 1.5M tokens billed at on-demand unless a pre-approved temporary burst addendum is in place).
- Grace/true-up: Standard commercial term is a 30-day invoice window plus a single-month true-up applied the next billing cycle; for multi-month chronic overages we discuss commit uplift at renewal.

Worked example (month 6 spike at 3x commit = 1.5M tokens):
- 500k tokens covered by commit @ $0.0008 = $400
- Next 500k (burst allowance / negotiated overage) @ $0.0012 = $600
- Final 500k (beyond burst cap) @ on-demand $0.0020 = $1,000
- Total for month 6 = $2,000 (vs. committed baseline $400). True-up: the $1,600 overage is invoiced per standard billing with 30-day payment terms; alternatively we can apply a one-time short-term burst credit on a case-by-case basis for first-time spikes (requires approval).

I'll attach the worksheet that models other scenarios and a SOW draft that includes a short burst addendum clause (we can move that to legal if you want). Copying Ben for pricing mechanics and Lauren for contract/renewal signals.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

2) For months with large spikes, would Redwood allow a 60-day true-up window if we provide forecast evidence and agree to an uplifted commit for the next quarter?

Ana — appreciate the clarity. A few practical guardrails from our side:
- Quarterly cap: we can add a soft cap where no more than 50% of total quarterly consumption can be billed at on-demand rates without a formal commit change. In practice that translates to a limit on sustained extended bursts.
- 60-day true-up: we generally operate on 30-day true-ups, but will make an exception to 45 days for first-year customers with forecast support; 60 days requires legal/credit sign-off.
- Invoice wording: we can include a line item labeled "Usage True-up (over commit)" with quantity in tokens and unit price, and a supporting CSV of per-day usage attached. That meets typical accounting requirements.

Ben Carter

Ana — appreciate the specifics. I spoke with legal and finance; proposed contract language we can add to SOW (summary):
- Burst allowance: defined as up to 2x monthly commit. Billing tiers within a month: Commit buckets billed first, burst bucket billed at negotiated overage rate (1.5x committed), excess beyond burst billed at on-demand.
- Escalation/notifications: Redwood will send automated consumption alerts at 80%, 100%, and 150% of commit; the account team will also reach out for >100% sustained usage for more than 7 days to discuss temporary uplift.
- First-spike credit: Redwood will provide a one-time 25% credit on the overage portion of the first spike month. Credit will be applied as an invoice credit in the next billing cycle.
- True-up window: 45 days for initial term (as an exception), returning to standard 30 days thereafter. 60 days requires credit review.

Next steps: Neha — if you can confirm sign-off for the pricing worksheet and I'll incorporate this language into SOW v2 for signature. Ben/Rishi — please confirm the negotiated overage rate (1.5x) and the quarterly soft cap language.

Thanks,
